summary: Manitowoc's city-owned power plant released about 9,200 lb to the air in 2024, mostly hydrochloric acid from burning fuel.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: About 7,200 lb of hydrochloric acid and 2,000 lb of ammonia went into the air. Both irritate the eyes, nose and lungs. Sources disagree on its fuel: federal energy data lists mostly wood and wood waste, but the utility said in 2025 that its two main boilers still burn mostly coal and petroleum coke. It is converting them to pellets made from paper and plastic waste.

avoid.label: Check air quality
avoid.text: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days

avoid.label: Kids play indoors
avoid.text: Keep kids with asthma indoors when the air quality index is orange or worse

avoid.label: Follow the changes
avoid.text: Follow MPU's switch to cleaner fuel at city utility meetings

impacts.title: Soil & gardens
impacts.where: Yards and gardens near the plant
impacts.how: The plant also released 3 lb of lead compounds. Lead doesn't break down: it settles onto soil and stays there, and small children are the most at risk.

avoid.label: Test garden soil
avoid.text: Test garden soil for lead before growing food near the plant

avoid.label: Wash hands
avoid.text: Wash vegetables and hands after gardening

avoid.label: Shoes off inside
avoid.text: Take shoes off at the door so soil dust stays outside
